doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Don Elliott, 'Counterpoint for Six Valves' and no royalties
summary: Riverside's duet record with Don Elliott and the NBC rhythm section, paid flat union scale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I have one copy. Does it say that really?
It does say that, yeah, I’ll show it to you. It’s interesting.
Yeah. Dick was on it. I wouldn’t do anything without him, it was that kind of a relationship.
How did your association with Don Elliott come about?

Well Riverside Records was a very well respected jazz label, like Keynote, and there were others that go way back. And I recorded for Keynote under my own name and they went bankrupt. Well Riverside didn’t go bankrupt. And Dick had a call to do something for them and it was his concept. And he said he’d like to do, that was that thing called “Counterpoint for Six Valves.” He’d like to do that and he wrote up some little duets and he picked me and Don Elliott to be the players. And the rhythm section was known at that time as the NBC rhythm section because they were all on staff. That was Mondello, Dick Hyman, Don Lamond and Eddie Safranski. And we just went in and played. That was kind of well received critically. It was a good record.
Did you get any kind of — I’m not sure of the word — from the number of records sold—
Did that make a difference to you or were you just paid from the beginning?
Flat union scale. Royalty you’re thinking of.
